To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
i) Dnn's generalization error is related to the Fourier spectrum of the target function; ii) Small initial values are helpful to achieve good generalization ability.

(1) the training of a DNN can be viewed as a low-pass filtering process, (2) the training of DNNs can be viewed as an iterative process that progressively filters high frequency components of the target functions, and (3) the training of the DNNs can also be viewed as an adaptive process that gradually increases the frequency range of the target functions that can be learned.

(1) The low frequency components of the target functions are endowed with a higher priority in the training process; and (2) Small initialization leads DNNs to have a higher priority to fit the low frequency components of target functions and thus to achieve better generalization performance.
